result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the screen-versus-ink limit and give solid next steps: a spot ink, the right paper and a physical proof. B is clearer about expectations ('expect some difference'), offers the useful tip of keeping black ink out of the orange, and uses slightly less jargon. A is thorough but leans on software and profile details (SWOP, GRACoL, Proof Colors, gamut warnings, CMYK builds) that a bakery owner will struggle to follow, and it never clearly says an exact match isn't possible. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain the gamut limit, separate it from things the bakery can control, and recommend a spot color and a physical proof on the actual paper. A is more honest that some difference remains ("expect some difference") and is easier for a non-designer to follow. B calls the problem fixable without saying an exact match is impossible, and its CMYK and Illustrator instructions are heavy on jargon for a bakery owner, though its point about lighting is useful.
